A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PA-VAD with the same CA-PAG and DARM components. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary materials are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and document template.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation-quality measurements, anomaly-detection results on ShanghaiTech and UCF-Crime, component ablations, and synthesized-data sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds XD-Violence evaluation, detector-space feature measurements, and open-set experiments with variability across class splits.

M1.justification: The CLIP-based image selection, VLM prompt refinement, diffusion generation, and DARM architecture and losses are retained. Scene balancing was already described in v1; v2 clarifies its application without establishing a new algorithmic component or changed detector procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds XD-Violence alongside ShanghaiTech and UCF-Crime. It also introduces restricted-class training and evaluation including unseen anomaly classes on UCF-Crime and XD-Violence, substantially broadening the tested scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 4 removes HF2-VAD, RTFM, and UMIL from the main comparison and adds PA-VAD using Sultani's classifier. New Tables 7–9 include Cai et al.'s RTFM/LAP variants, SF-VAD/FPL, and OpenVAD. RTFM reappears specifically in the open-set UCF-Crime comparison.

E3.justification: New open-set protocols use 1/3/6/9 seen classes on UCF-Crime and 1/4 on XD-Violence, followed by full-test evaluation. XD introduces its 3,954/800 training/test split and 60 pseudo-abnormal plus 50 pseudo-normal clips. The appendix changes UCF-Crime's stated batch size from 4 to 32; whether retained experiments were rerun is unspecified.

E4.justification: v2 adds a randomly selected initial-image baseline, Qwen/C3D feature-norm comparisons in Table 1, and detector-space measurements with domain alignment alone versus full DARM in Table 5b. Tables 8–9 newly test unseen-class robustness. The earlier component ablations and pseudo-clip-count analysis remain.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty. For the new open-set experiments, v2 reports mean AUC and standard deviation over three random class splits. This adds localized variability reporting without establishing additional runs for the retained benchmark results.

E6.justification: New results include XD-Violence AUC of 95.1 with DARM versus 92.5 with UR-DMU, open-set outcomes, an 86.7 SHT random-image baseline, and detector-space norms. Headline SHT/UCF-Crime values remain 98.2/82.5. MGSTRL's SHT score changes from 85.1 to 87.5, overtaking SeeKer; HSC's UCF-Crime and Sultani's SHT entries disappear. Unchanged Table 3 values now have correctly calculated FVD/KVD reductions in the prose.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation is substantively unchanged. v2 numbers the previously inline memory-normalization definition and clarifies negative-prompt notation, but adds no new mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim of effective detection without real abnormal training videos remains. v2 adds an explicit unseen-class generalization claim in the abstract and introduction and extends its claimed benchmark success to XD-Violence, while retaining the original main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's assertion of a fully fair UVAD comparison with a qualification about additional pretrained generative and vision-language priors. It adds interpretations of detector-space magnitude amplification, abnormal-prototype correction, and usage-aware updates as protection against seen-class overfitting. The existing long-context generation limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies detector backbones in Table 4, states that prior-method scores are quoted, and adds XD hyperparameters, guidance settings, and generation costs. The appendix revises the hardware description from one 100 GB GPU to two 96 GB GPUs and updates UCF-Crime's batch size. These are documentation changes; hardware changes or reruns are not independently established.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion concerning SF-VAD/FPL, OpenVAD, DANN, I3D/C3D, and XD-Violence, and removes VideoCrafter2. It also describes Rai et al.'s pretrained-diffusion inpainting more precisely. The broader positioning against UVAD, WVAD, and anomaly-synthesis approaches is retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and portions of the introduction and experimental discussion are rewritten; author order and method/appendix headings also change. The overall section sequence and much of the explanatory prose remain, with new scientific content accounting for much of the expansion.

P2.justification: v2 switches from two-column to single-column layout and extensively resizes and relocates material. It merges v1 Figures 4–5 into Figure 4, restructures Tables 1, 4, and 5, adds comparison Tables 7–9, and adds an XD-Violence example to the supplementary video figure.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the proposed mechanism and generalization. Detector-space controls in Table 5b directly investigate the magnitude correction previously supported mainly by accuracy ablations and frozen-feature statistics. Open-set experiments with split variability address previously untested category transfer, while the supervision caveat improves interpretive accuracy. Some main baselines are removed, and attributing open-set gains specifically to DARM remains unablated, but the new evidence provides a substantial overall improvement.
